brief: GS's Weekly Kickstart argues falling equity positioning (Sentiment Indicator at -0.9, matching March lows, and asset manager equity length down from 48% to 36% of futures open interest) has driven market breadth to its narrowest since the Dot-Com Bubble, with the median S&P 500 stock 16% below its 52-week high even as AI strength keeps the index near highs. GS reads this as potential for broad upside and a laggard catch-up if macro uncertainty fades. The equity risk premium sits near 3%, and current valuations imply a 22% ROE, 2pp below the trailing level, reflecting skepticism that AI-driven profitability is sustainable. GS's Value factor, up over 25% since mid-2025, now has a weaker outlook given narrow valuation dispersion. Separately, GS forecasts near-term core CPI acceleration (September +0.24%, October +0.22%, boosted by airfares, energy costs and BLS residual seasonality tied to last year's shutdown) before cooling to +0.11% by December, while core PCE stays stickier. On the tape, oil's surge and hot flash PMIs pushed the 30-year Treasury yield to its highest since 2004, though a reported Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and an extended US-China trade truce marked by Xi's Washington visit offered late-week relief.
